sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·韦丹塔姆。

sentences.en: You don't have to look far to see evidence of narcissism in our culture.
sentences.zh: 不用看太远，你就能在我们文化中看到自恋的证据。

sentences.en: I'm an international phenomenon and my name is Miley and everyone knows that.
sentences.zh: 我是个国际巨星，我的名字叫麦莉，人人都知道这一点。

sentences.en: No, no, I know that.
sentences.zh: 不，不，我知道。

sentences.en: Snap, girls.
sentences.zh: 太棒了，女孩们。

sentences.en: The show's over.
sentences.zh: 节目结束了。

sentences.en: You can all go home.
sentences.zh: 你们都可以回家了。

sentences.en: Pack your bags.
sentences.zh: 收拾好行李吧。

sentences.en: I have not done a selfie in this glam room.
sentences.zh: 我还没在这个化妆间里自拍过呢。

sentences.en: How many selfies are you going to do in one day?
sentences.zh: 你一天要拍多少张自拍？

sentences.en: You're like obsessed.
sentences.zh: 你简直着了魔一样。

sentences.en: I just need, I need 1,200.
sentences.zh: 我只需要，我需要1200张。

sentences.en: Kanye West and Kim Kardashian are only the tip of the iceberg.
sentences.zh: 坎耶·韦斯特和金·卡戴珊只是冰山一角。

sentences.en: Our society is in the midst of a full-blown narcissism epidemic.
sentences.zh: 我们的社会正处于全面的自恋流行病之中。

sentences.en: It doesn't take a psychologist to see that, but we decided to talk to one anyway.
sentences.zh: 不需要心理学家就能看出这一点，但我们还是决定跟一位心理学家聊聊。

sentences.en: We're more focused on the self.
sentences.zh: 我们更加关注自我。

sentences.en: We're less focused on social rules.
sentences.zh: 我们对社会规则的关注减少了。

sentences.en: At the extreme, that can turn into this narcissistic attention-seeking of everybody.
sentences.zh: 在极端情况下，这会演变成所有人那种自恋的博眼球行为。

sentences.en: Look at me and how great I am.
sentences.zh: 看看我，我是多么伟大。

sentences.en: This is Jean Twenge.
sentences.zh: 这位是简·特温杰。

sentences.en: She's a psychologist at San Diego State.
sentences.zh: 她是圣迭戈州立大学的心理学家。

sentences.en: She's analyzed data collected from millions of people over the last half century.
sentences.zh: 她分析了过去半个世纪里从数百万收集到的数据。

sentences.en: We found that if you look at baby boomers in the 60s compared to millennials in more recent times,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，如果你把60年代的婴儿潮一代与近年来的千禧一代进行比较，

sentences.en: millennials are much more likely to say that they think they're above average.
sentences.zh: 千禧一代更有可能认为自己高于平均水平。

sentences.en: We'll talk about what this means for young people later in the conversation,
sentences.zh: 我们稍后会在对话中探讨这对年轻人意味着什么，

sentences.en: but Jean Twenge says our culture as a whole, from reality TV to social media,
sentences.zh: 但简·特温杰表示，从真人秀到社交媒体，我们的整个文化

sentences.en: has come to encourage an obsessive focus on the self.
sentences.zh: 开始助长一种对自我的痴迷关注。

sentences.en: I think there are a lot of factors.
sentences.zh: 我认为有很多因素。

sentences.en: You know, our culture has changed in so many ways.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们的文化在很多方面都发生了变化。

sentences.en: And the feature that I always come back to is we are a more individualistic culture now
sentences.zh: 而我总是回归的一个特点是，我们现在是一个更加个人主义的文化，

sentences.en: compared to what our culture was, say, in the 1950s.
sentences.zh: 相比于比如说20世纪50年代我们的文化。

sentences.en: So we're more focused on the self.
sentences.zh: 所以我们更加关注自我。

sentences.en: We're less focused on social rules.
sentences.zh: 我们对社会规则的关注减少了。

sentences.en: At the extreme, that can turn into this narcissistic attention-seeking of everybody.
sentences.zh: 在极端情况下，这会演变成所有人那种自恋的博眼球行为。

sentences.en: Look at me and how great I am.
sentences.zh: 看看我，我是多么伟大。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering if this affects not just the people at the extreme ends of the spectrum,
sentences.zh: 我想知道这是否不仅影响了处于极端频谱的人，

sentences.en: but people who are, you know, the rest of us.
sentences.zh: 还影响了其他人，也就是你我这样的大多数人。

sentences.en: You have Facebook and Twitter and all kinds of mechanisms now to tell people
sentences.zh: 你现在有了Facebook、Twitter以及各种各样的机制去告诉别人

sentences.en: what you had for dinner last night, what wonderful vacation you're going on,
sentences.zh: 你昨晚吃了什么晚饭，你要去度什么美妙的假期，

sentences.en: the amazing things that your kid is doing at school.
sentences.zh: 你的孩子在学校里做了什么了不起的事。

sentences.en: There are all kinds of ways to boast about yourself to more and more people.
sentences.zh: 有各种各样的方式向越来越多的人吹嘘你自己。

sentences.en: Yeah, social networking really pulls forward the positive.
sentences.zh: 是的，社交网络确实把积极的一面放大了。

sentences.en: It really encourages people to just focus on the good parts of themselves.
sentences.zh: 它确实鼓励人们只关注自己好的一面。

sentences.en: Which, you know, in some ways is the definition of narcissism.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，这正是自恋的定义。

sentences.en: Now, I'm not saying everybody on these sites is narcissistic per se,
sentences.zh: 当然，我并不是说这些网站上的每个人本质上都是自恋的，

sentences.en: but we do know from lots of studies now, five or six,
sentences.zh: 但我们从现在的大量研究（大约五六项）中确实知道，

sentences.en: that people who score high in narcissism have more friends on Facebook, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，自恋得分高的人在Facebook上有更多的好友。

sentences.en: So the average person you're connected to on one of these sites
sentences.zh: 所以，你在这些网站上联系的平均一个人，

sentences.en: is probably higher in narcissism than the average person you know in real life.
sentences.zh: 他的自恋程度可能比你在现实生活中认识的平均一个人要高。

sentences.en: And that molds the way people communicate in a way that really does seek attention,
sentences.zh: 这塑造了人们的交流方式，让他们确实在寻求关注，

sentences.en: especially for all of these positive things.
sentences.zh: 尤其是为了所有这些积极的事情。

sentences.en: It is really a venue for bragging that just wasn't available 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 这确实是一个炫耀的平台，是20年前所没有的。

sentences.en: I'm fascinated by one point that you make in your book,
sentences.zh: 我对你在书中提出的一个观点很着迷，

sentences.en: which is a lot of this might start very early with a cultural emphasis on building self-esteem
sentences.zh: 那就是这一切很大程度上可能很早就开始了，伴随着文化对建立自尊的强调

sentences.en: and on encouraging young people to follow their dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 以及对鼓励年轻人追随梦想的重视。

sentences.en: And at one level, that statement seems almost anodyne,
sentences.zh: 从某种层面上看，这种说法似乎无可厚非，

sentences.en: that it's a good thing to encourage people to follow their dreams,
sentences.zh: 即鼓励人们追随梦想是一件好事，

sentences.en: to encourage people to believe in themselves and believe in what they're capable of doing.
sentences.zh: 鼓励人们相信自己，相信自己有能力做到。

sentences.en: But you raise a number of examples or a number of concerns about the potential downside
sentences.zh: 但你提出了许多例子或担忧，关于鼓励人们相信自己并追随梦想的潜在负面影响。

sentences.en: of encouraging people to believe in themselves and follow their dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 能稍微谈谈这个吗？

sentences.en: Talk about that a little bit.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我们可以在文化中看到这一点。

sentences.en: So, yes, we can see this in the culture.
sentences.zh: 社会非常强调对自己感觉良好，即积极的自我认知。

sentences.en: There is this very strong emphasis on feeling good about yourself, positive self-views.
sentences.zh: 这体现在很多短语中，比如，

sentences.en: It's captured in a lot of phrases like,
sentences.zh: 你想成为什么样的人就能成为什么样的人，追随你的梦想，你是特别的。

sentences.en: you can be anything you want to be, follow your dreams, you are special.
sentences.zh: 相信自己，一切皆有可能。

sentences.en: Believe in yourself and anything is possible.
sentences.zh: 人们认为理所当然的是，要想成功，你必须拥有极高的自尊。

sentences.en: It is taken for granted that to succeed, you must have very high self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 但问题在于，许多研究表明事实并非如此。

sentences.en: The problem with that is it's not true from many studies.
sentences.zh: 所以，一项大型研究综述探讨了这一点。

sentences.en: So, big research review looked at this.
sentences.zh: 自尊得分高的人并不一定比其他人更成功，

sentences.en: And people who score high in self-esteem are not necessarily any more successful than anybody else,
sentences.zh: 特别是当你把家庭背景之类的因素考虑在内时。

sentences.en: especially when you take into account family background and things like that.
sentences.zh: 你确实会发现一些效应，例如，在学校表现出色的孩子会建立高自尊。

sentences.en: You do find some effect that, for example, kids who do well in school develop high self-esteem.
sentences.zh: 但我们文化中的看法是，你应该无缘无故地建立自尊。

sentences.en: But the way our culture thinks about it is you should build up self-esteem for no particular reason.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为你是你，你就是特别的。

sentences.en: You're special just for being you.
sentences.zh: 这就会带来美好的结果。

sentences.en: And that will lead to good things.
sentences.zh: 事实并非如此。

sentences.en: It doesn't work that way.
sentences.zh: 那是本末倒置。

sentences.en: That puts the cart before the horse.
sentences.zh: 我想知道它是否会产生更具破坏性的影响，

sentences.en: I'm wondering if it might even have an even more pernicious effect than that,
sentences.zh: 那就是如果你在没有真正取得成就以及没有付出必要努力的情况下建立自尊，

sentences.en: which is that if you build up your self-esteem without actually the accomplishments and the effort required to build it up in a genuine fashion,
sentences.zh: 它实际上可能会阻碍你去做出真正能带来成就的事情。

sentences.en: it might actually dissuade you from doing the things that would actually lead to achievements.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你的自尊本来就已经高耸入云时，你还有什么心理动力去努力工作并取得能建立自尊的成就呢？

sentences.en: I mean, what psychological incentive do you have to work hard and achieve things that can build up your self-esteem when your self-esteem is sky high to begin with?
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 但这确实通过一个数据证明了这种观点：认为要想成功就必须极其自信，这种想法根本不是真的。

sentences.en: But it really does really demonstrate in one piece of data how this idea that you have to be supremely self-confident to succeed just isn't true.
sentences.zh: 你在书中引用了谷歌图书的数据，观察了“你可以成为任何人”这一短语在一段时间内的使用情况。

sentences.en: You cite data in the book looking at Google Books and the use of the phrase, you can be anything, over a period of time.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 所以我们查看了谷歌图书数据库中的个人主义词汇和短语。

sentences.en: So we looked at individualistic words and phrases in the Google Books database.
sentences.zh: 我们还查看了诸如“我”和“我的”与“我们”和“我们的”之类的人称代词，试图了解关于语言使用的这种更广泛的文化观点，

sentences.en: We also looked at pronouns like I and me versus we and us to try to see this more broader cultural view about language use
sentences.zh: 以及这在过去50或60年中可能发生了怎样的变化。

sentences.en: and how that might have changed over the last 50 or 60 years.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的资源。

sentences.en: This is a great resource.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到——我们查看了美国书籍，发现向更具个人主义的语言转变的趋势非常明显。

sentences.en: You can look at – we looked at American books and found a pretty pronounced shift toward more individualistic language.
sentences.zh: 所以“你是特别的”。

sentences.en: So you are special.
sentences.zh: “我是最棒的”。

sentences.en: I'm the beSt.
sentences.zh: 所有这些短语都增加了。

sentences.en: All of those phrases went up.
sentences.zh: 像“独特”和“个性化”这样的词也是如此。

sentences.en: Words like unique and personalized.
sentences.zh: “我”以及对“我”、“我的”的使用增加了。

sentences.en: I and the use of I, me, and mine went up.
sentences.zh: “我们”和“我们的”的使用略有下降。

sentences.en: The use of we and us went down by a little bit.
sentences.zh: 增幅最大的一项是对“你”和“你的”的使用。

sentences.en: One of the biggest increases was the use of you and yours.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，作者直接与读者对话的方式增加了。

sentences.en: So a way that the author is directly speaking to the reader.
sentences.zh: 所以这全都是非常个人主义的语言。

sentences.en: So all very individualistic language.
sentences.zh: 它确实表明，这不仅仅是代际转变，而是演变成了更强调个人的整体文化转变。

sentences.en: And it really shows how it goes beyond just this generational shift toward an overall cultural shift that is emphasizing the individual more.
sentences.zh: 你探讨了这样一个事实：这一切从父母给孩子起名字的那一刻就开始了。

sentences.en: You explore the fact this begins right from the point at which parents give names to children.
sentences.zh: 是的，另一个精美的大型数据集是社会保障局的婴儿姓名数据集。

sentences.en: Yeah, so another nice, beautiful, big data set, the Social Security Administration baby names data set.
sentences.zh: 很多人对此很熟悉，因为它们会告诉你哪些名字最受欢迎。

sentences.en: Many people are familiar with this because they'll tell you which names are the most popular.
sentences.zh: 我们感兴趣的是有多少婴儿拥有受欢迎的名字。

sentences.en: We were interested in how many babies get popular names.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，获得例如前10名中最受欢迎名字的婴儿比例发生了显著变化。

sentences.en: And we found a pronounced shift in the percentage of babies who get, for example, one of the top 10 names.
sentences.zh: 早在50年代，大约三分之一的男孩和25%的女孩仅仅使用了那10个最受欢迎的名字。

sentences.en: Back in the 50s, about a third of boys and about 25% of girls got just those 10 most popular names.
sentences.zh: 而现在这一比例不到10%。

sentences.en: And now it's less than 10%.
sentences.zh: 所以过去父母会给孩子起常见的名字，这样他们就能融入集体，因为这被认为是一件好事。

sentences.en: So it used to be that parents would give kids common names so they could fit in because that was considered a good thing.
sentences.zh: 现在，重点是让我们给孩子起一个独特的名，以便他或她能脱颖而出。

sentences.en: Now the emphasis is let's give our child a unique name so he or she can stand out.
sentences.zh: 这再次捕捉到了对独特性质的强调，而独特性是个人主义不可或缺的一部分。

sentences.en: And that, again, captures that emphasis on uniqueness, which is an integral part of individualism.
sentences.zh: 向更大程度的个人主义转变的文化对特定的一群人——年轻人，也就是被称为千禧一代的这一代人——产生了深远的影响。

sentences.en: The cultural shift toward greater individualism has had a profound effect on one group in particular, young people, the generation known as the millennials.
sentences.zh: 简·特温杰分析了半个世纪以来收集的调查数据，这些数据向年轻人提出了许多问题，以衡量他们的自恋水平。

sentences.en: Jean Twenge has analyzed survey data collected over a half century that asks young people a number of questions to measure their levels of narcissism.
sentences.zh: 其中一个问题是：与同龄人相比，你认为自己高于平均水平吗？

sentences.en: So one is to say, do you think that you're above average compared to other people your age?
sentences.zh: 然后会给出一系列特质。

sentences.en: And then there's a list of traits given.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，如果你把60年代的婴儿潮一代与近年来的千禧一代进行比较，

sentences.en: And we found that if you look at baby boomers in the 60s compared to millennials in more recent times,
sentences.zh: 千禧一代更有可能认为自己在进取心、领导能力、写作能力、一般学术能力等特质上高于平均水平。

sentences.en: millennials are much more likely to say that they think they're above average in traits like drive to achieve, leadership ability, writing ability, general academic ability.
sentences.zh: 全面来看，他们会说，是的，我觉得我在这些方面比我这个年纪的其他人更好。

sentences.en: Across the board, they say, yeah, I think I'm better than other people my age at this.
sentences.zh: 我们想知道这是否是人口结构变化导致的。

sentences.en: And we wondered if it was demographic shifts.
sentences.zh: 我们发现，并不是这样的。

sentences.en: We found out, no, that it wasn't.
sentences.zh: 现在大学群体中更显著的群体在诸如此类的测量中得分实际上更低。

sentences.en: The groups that are more prominent in college populations now actually score lower on measures like that.
sentences.zh: 我们想知道这是否是实际表现，但也不是。

sentences.en: We wondered if it was actual performance, but it's not.
sentences.zh: SAT分数保持不变或有所下降。

sentences.en: SAT scores are unchanged or down.
sentences.zh: 但我们确实从另一个来源找到了证据，那就是观察这些学生在高中时获得的反馈类型，即他们的成绩。

sentences.en: But we did find evidence from another source to see the type of feedback that these students are given when they're in high school, their grades.
sentences.zh: 高中以A平均分毕业的百分比翻了一番，这是捕捉对自我感觉良好之强调的另一种方式。

sentences.en: And the percentage you graduate with an A average from high school has doubled, which is another way that captures this emphasis that's placed on feeling good about yourself.
sentences.zh: 因为如果有更多的人是A等生，更多的人就会对自己感觉良好，尽管表现其实差不多。

sentences.en: Because if more people are A students, more people feel good about themselves, even though performance is about the same.
sentences.zh: 而高中生花在家庭作业上的时间实际上减少了。

sentences.en: And the amount of time high school students spend on homework has actually gone down.
sentences.zh: 所以并不是他们工作更努力了。

sentences.en: So it's not that they're working harder.
sentences.zh: 我想知道我是否可以反驳你一会儿。

sentences.en: I wonder if I can push back at you for just a moment.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你想到年轻人更加个人主义、对自己的期望更加自信时，我也能看到这有非常积极的一面。

sentences.en: You know, when you think about young people being more individualistic, being more assertive about their own expectations, I can also see this having a really good side to it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果我想到今天的年轻女性，我想象年轻女性对雇主、对浪漫伴侣、对，

sentences.en: You know, if I'm thinking about young women today, I would imagine that young women probably have higher expectations about their employers, about their romantic partners, about,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，与她们互动的人，可能会有更高的期望，她们对应该属于自己的东西更加自信。

sentences.en: you know, who they interact with, that they're more assertive about the things that should be coming to them.
sentences.zh: 我想象这肯定是一件好事。

sentences.en: And I would imagine that this has to be a good thing.
sentences.zh: 是的，真有趣你会提到这个，因为我就是这样开始研究整个代际问题的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's funny you'd mention that because that's how I got into this whole generational thing in the first place.
sentences.zh: 我做的前几项研究是关于女性人格特质和角色的变化。

sentences.en: The first few studies that I did were looking at changes in women's personality traits and roles.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们所发现的，女性变得更加自信，更加关注领导力。

sentences.en: And that's exactly what we found, that women have become more assertive, more focused on leadership.
sentences.zh: 我认为在一定限度内，这是一件好事，我们有了更多的性别平等，

sentences.en: And I think within limits, that is a good thing, that we have more gender equality,
sentences.zh: 我们有了更愿意自信的女性，而且这在社会上更容易被接受。

sentences.en: that we have women who are more willing to be assertive and that that's more socially acceptable.
sentences.zh: 当我写那前几篇论文时，我的看法是，这绝对是一件好事。

sentences.en: And when I did those first few papers, that was my view, that that was an unmitigated good.
sentences.zh: 然后随着我的研究继续，我开始研究自尊和自恋以及一些更极端的表现，我意识到这是一个权衡，

sentences.en: And then as my research went on and I started to look at self-esteem and narcissism and some of the more extreme forms, I realized that it was a tradeoff,
sentences.zh: 拥有一些自信和自我信赖是一件很好的事情，但这也完全有可能做得过头。

sentences.en: that it can be a very good thing to have some assertiveness and some self-confidence, but that it is also very possible for that to be taken too far.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是自信，而是过度自信。

sentences.en: Not just confidence, but overconfidence.
sentences.zh: 所以当它转变成那种过度膨胀的自我意识时——这也是自恋的一种定义，这时候就会出现问题。

sentences.en: So when it crosses into that overinflated sense of self, which is one definition of narcissism, that's when it can be problematic.
sentences.zh: 不过我必须说，这可能不仅限于35岁及以下的人群，他们正处于总统大选中，里面有很多候选人在说，

sentences.en: I have to say, though, that this might not be limited to the 35 and under crowd who are in the midst of a presidential election where there are a lot of candidates who are saying,
sentences.zh: 你知道，看着我。

sentences.en: you know, look at me.
sentences.zh: 我是最棒的。

sentences.en: I'm the beSt.
sentences.zh: 在我领导下事情会变得非常棒。

sentences.en: Things are going to be great under me.
sentences.zh: 我知道我在做什么。

sentences.en: I know what I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 我知道得比别人多。

sentences.en: I know better than other people.
sentences.zh: 这确实...

sentences.en: You don't see a lot of careful reflection and self-doubt and caution and, you know, other people know better than I do.
sentences.zh: 你看不到太多认真的反思、自我怀疑、谨慎，以及那种“你知道的，别人比我更懂”的心态。

sentences.en: You don't hear a lot of that.
sentences.zh: 你很少听到这种说法。

sentences.en: You hear a lot of bragging.
sentences.zh: 你听到更多的是吹嘘。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there's actually a study that looked indirectly at presidential narcissism.
sentences.zh: 所以，实际上有一项研究间接探讨了总统的自恋倾向。

sentences.en: They looked at historians' depictions of their personality and coded these on a rubric that lined up with narcissistic personality.
sentences.zh: 他们研究了历史学家对这些总统个性的描述，并根据与自恋型人格相吻合的评分标准进行了编码。

sentences.en: And sure enough, our presidents are a narcissistic bunch compared to the average American.
sentences.zh: 果不其然，与普通美国人相比，我们的总统是一群相当自恋的人。

sentences.en: But also that's grown over time.
sentences.zh: 而且这种现象随着时间推移还在加剧。

sentences.en: More recent presidents are higher.
sentences.zh: 更年轻的总统得分更高。

sentences.en: In those narcissistic traits compared to previous decades.
sentences.zh: 与过去几十年相比，他们在这些自恋特质上表现得更明显。

sentences.en: Some of that is just the media pulls for this.
sentences.zh: 部分原因只是媒体推波助澜的结果。

sentences.en: That in a time when really what a presidential election is about is a public performance, it's not really about caring for other people.
sentences.zh: 在一个总统竞选的核心实际上是公众表演的时代，它其实并不是关于关心他人。

sentences.en: It's about a public performance.
sentences.zh: 这全关乎公众表演。

sentences.en: That pulls for more narcissistic personality.
sentences.zh: 这会促生更多自恋型的人格。

sentences.en: Psychologist Jean Twenge, when we come back, Jean and I will talk about the downside of making young people feel that they are wildly special.
sentences.zh: 心理学家让·特温格，等我们回来后，我和让将探讨让年轻人觉得自己极其特别所带来的消极影响。

sentences.en: When you talk to millennials, you can really see this disillusionment that they were set up with this very buoyant view of what their future was going to be.
sentences.zh: 当你与千禧一代交谈时，你真的能看到这种幻灭感，他们被灌输了一种对未来极其乐观的美好愿景。

sentences.en: And they ended up disappointed by what they found when they got to adulthood.
sentences.zh: 结果当他们步入成年时，现实却让他们感到失望。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Jean Twenge, you've painted a disturbing picture about rising levels of narcissism, personal ambition, and individualism.
sentences.zh: 让·特温格，你描绘了一幅令人担忧的图景，关于不断上升的自恋水平、个人野心和个人主义。

sentences.en: What happens when people's sky-high impressions of themselves and their expectations, their self-image, what happens when all these things collide with reality?
sentences.zh: 当人们对自己极高的印象和期望、他们的自我形象，当所有这些与现实发生碰撞时，会发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, it can be a difficult picture.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这可能会是一幅艰难的画卷。

sentences.en: So just for a little background firSt.
sentences.zh: 所以先做一点背景介绍。

sentences.en: We know from these surveys of high school students, for example, that twice as many expect to get, for example, a graduate and professional degree compared to boomers in the 70s.
sentences.zh: 例如，我们从这些对高中生的调查中得知，期望获得研究生和专业学位的人数是70年代垮掉的一代（婴儿潮一代）的两倍。

sentences.en: Yet the same number of people will actually get those degrees.
sentences.zh: 然而，最终真正获得这些学位的人数其实是一样的。

sentences.en: So expectations have grown and reality has stayed about the same.
sentences.zh: 因此，期望值提高了，而现实却基本保持不变。

sentences.en: So at some point, these expectations collide with reality.
sentences.zh: 所以在某个时刻，这些期望与现实发生了碰撞。

sentences.en: And that can potentially lead to unhappiness and it can potentially lead to anxiety and depression and other mental health issues.
sentences.zh: 这可能会导致不快乐，并可能引发焦虑、抑郁和其他心理健康问题。

sentences.en: So we looked at this with happiness recently and we found a decline in happiness among adults age 30 and older, especially in the last 10 or 15 years.
sentences.zh: 因此，我们最近就幸福感进行了研究，发现30岁及以上的成年人的幸福感有所下降，尤其是在过去10到15年里。

sentences.en: And that may be partially due to these expectations not being met.
sentences.zh: 这可能部分是因为这些期望没有得到满足。

sentences.en: So you're finding something actually quite profoundly sad here,
sentences.zh: 所以你在这里发现了一些实际上非常深刻且令人悲伤的事情，

sentences.en: which is it's not just that this culture of individualism is not necessarily helping us when it comes to achievement,
sentences.zh: 那就是，这种个人主义文化不仅在涉及成就时不见得对我们有帮助，

sentences.en: but it might actually be counterproductive when it comes to our mental health and our happiness.
sentences.zh: 而且在我们的心理健康和幸福感方面，它实际上可能是适得其反的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you know, the happiness picture was especially interesting because adolescents are actually happier.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，幸福感的状况特别有趣，因为青少年的幸福感实际上更高。

sentences.en: So they have the happy individualism and optimism compared to those, say, in the 90s.
sentences.zh: 因此，与比如90年代的人相比，他们拥有那种快乐的个人主义和乐观主义。

sentences.en: But then they hit this wall sometime in their mid-20s to 30 when then in recent times happiness is lower.
sentences.zh: 但随后他们在20多岁到30岁之间的某个时候碰壁了，近年来的幸福感反而降低了。

sentences.en: Because it used to be people over the age of 30 were significantly happier than those in their 20s.
sentences.zh: 因为过去30岁以上的人的幸福感明显高于20多岁的人。

sentences.en: And they still are, but by a much smaller margin than they used to be.
sentences.zh: 现在他们依然如此，但幅度比过去小得多了。

sentences.en: It used to be growing up, you became more content.
sentences.zh: 过去随着年龄增长，你会变得更加满足。

sentences.en: And that's not quite as true as it used to be.
sentences.zh: 而现在这已经不像过去那么真实了。

sentences.en: Then there's the bigger issue of anxiety and depression, and we see more of those issues coming up as well.
sentences.zh: 接着还有更严重的问题，那就是焦虑和抑郁，我们看到这些问题也越来越多地出现。

sentences.en: And even at younger ages, high school students now are more likely to say they have trouble sleeping, that they have trouble concentrating.
sentences.zh: 甚至在更小的年龄段，现在的受访高中生也更有可能表示自己有睡眠问题，有注意力不集中的问题。

sentences.en: And these are psychosomatic symptoms of depression.
sentences.zh: 而这些都是抑郁症的心身症状。

sentences.en: So there's a real irony here, isn't it,
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一个真正的讽刺之处，不是吗？

sentences.en: which is that the generation that has been taught you are special and can make a difference is reaching the conclusion that they are not special and they can't make a difference.
sentences.zh: 那就是被教导“你是特别的、能够改变世界”的那一代人，正在得出这样的结论：他们其实并不特别，也无法改变世界。

sentences.en: And that must be very, very painful.
sentences.zh: 那一定非常、非常痛苦。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我也这么认为。

sentences.en: And I think when you talk to millennials, you can really see this disillusionment and anger that they feel.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，当你和千禧一代交谈时，你真的能看到他们感受到的这种幻灭感和愤怒。

sentences.en: I think rightly so, that they were set up with this very buoyant view of what their future was going to be.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是理所当然的，他们被灌输了对未来极其乐观的看法。

sentences.en: And they, I mean, this was true even before the Great Recession hit, that they ended up disappointed by what they found when they got to adulthood.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，甚至在大衰退爆发之前就是如此，他们最终对成年后所面对的现实感到失望。

sentences.en: And then the economic picture changed for the worse, and it became an even more difficult transition to adulthood.
sentences.zh: 然后经济状况变得更糟，向成年期的过渡变得更加艰难。

sentences.en: I want to ask you a personal question.
sentences.zh: 我想问你一个私人的问题。

sentences.en: You have children yourself, and you've done a lot of research looking at the potential perils of teaching children to be overly individualistic or narcissistic.
sentences.zh: 你自己也有孩子，而且你做了很多研究，探讨教导孩子过于个人主义或自恋的潜在危险。

sentences.en: What are you doing to change the way your own children think?
sentences.zh: 你在做些什么来改变你自己的孩子的思维方式？

sentences.en: So we talk a lot about hard work.
sentences.zh: 所以我们经常谈论努力工作。

sentences.en: We don't talk a lot about feeling special at all.
sentences.zh: 我们根本不怎么谈论感觉自己很特别这回事。

sentences.en: It's funny.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: Some people will sometimes say to me, oh, do you tell your kids you're not special?
sentences.zh: 有时候有人会对我说：“哦，你会告诉你的孩子他们并不特别吗？”

sentences.en: Well, no.
sentences.zh: 嗯，并没有。

sentences.en: We just don't talk about it that much.
sentences.zh: 我们只是不怎么谈论这个。

sentences.en: When it does come up, my oldest one in particular, she does know what narcissism means.
sentences.zh: 当谈到这个时，尤其是我的大女儿，她确实知道自恋是什么意思。

sentences.en: And we've talked about that.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论过这个问题。

sentences.en: And so, you know, because she sees that.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道的，因为她能看到这一点。

sentences.en: She sees it around her.
sentences.zh: 她能在周围看到这一点。

sentences.en: She sees it in things that we see on TV.
sentences.zh: 她能在我们在电视上看到的内容中看到这一点。

sentences.en: And kind of knowing what that is has helped us, you know, have a dialogue about, you know, well, there's the things that are really important,
sentences.zh: 知道那是什么有助于我们，你知道的，开展一场对话，关于，你知道的，有些事情是非常重要的，

sentences.en: like having friends and doing well in school and spending time with their family.
sentences.zh: 比如拥有朋友、在学校表现良好以及花时间陪伴家人。

sentences.en: And then there's the things that people think are important that maybe aren't quite as important as everybody thinks they are,
sentences.zh: 然后还有一些人们认为重要但也许并不像每个人想象得那么重要的事情，

sentences.en: like getting lots of attention and looking perfect all the time.
sentences.zh: 比如获得大量关注和时刻看起来完美无瑕。

sentences.en: And then with my younger two, it's just more of a focus on I love you instead of you're special, which is what parents mean anyway.
sentences.zh: 然后对于我较小的两个孩子，更多的则是专注于“我爱你”而不是“你很特别”，这本来就是父母想表达的意思。

sentences.en: And then just really focusing on, okay, the way to get better is to work hard and that what you do does make a difference.
sentences.zh: 然后真正专注于：好吧，变得更好的方法是努力工作，你所做的事情确实能带来改变。

sentences.en: But it's not just how you feel about yourself.
sentences.zh: 但重要的不仅是你对自己的看法。

sentences.en: It's what you do.
sentences.zh: 而是你的所作所为。

sentences.en: What suggestions do you have for young people?
sentences.zh: 你对年轻人有什么建议？

sentences.en: We have a lot of millennials who listen to our podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们的播客有很多千禧一代的听众。

sentences.en: What do you think young people can do to both learn from this research but also apply its findings to their own lives?
sentences.zh: 你认为年轻人可以做些什么，既能从这项研究中学习，又能将其发现应用到他们自己的生活中？

sentences.en: So, you know, first, I really want folks to understand none of this is meant at all as a criticism and it's not about blaming.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，首先，我真的很希望大家明白，所有这些都不是批评的意思，也无关指责。

sentences.en: It's about what young people have to say and how is that different from what previous generations said when they were the same age.
sentences.zh: 这是关于年轻人要表达什么，以及这与前人在他们同龄时所表达的有什么不同。

sentences.en: What can we learn from that?
sentences.zh: 我们能从中学到什么？

sentences.en: How can we take that and understand, you know, have a clear-eyed view of the changes in our culture?
sentences.zh: 我们如何从中汲取经验并理解，你知道的，对我们文化的变迁有一个清醒的认识？

sentences.en: So, I think every generation – I'm a Gen Xer, so we did the same thing.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为每一代人——我是X世代，所以我们也做过同样的事。

sentences.en: You know, we looked at our culture.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们审视我们的文化。

sentences.en: We looked at ourselves and said, hey, you know, there's some things here that need to change and there's some things here we want to keep.
sentences.zh: 我们审视自己，然后说：嘿，你知道的，这里有些事情需要改变，这里有些事情我们想要保留。

sentences.en: And I think every generation does that.
sentences.zh: 我想每一代人都会这么做。

sentences.en: So, my hope is that millennials will do that and say, hey, you know, maybe I'm not going to tell my kids that they're so special and that they can be anything.
sentences.zh: 所以，我希望千禧一代也能这样做，然后说：嘿，你知道的，也许我不会告诉我的孩子们他们是多么特别、他们可以成为任何想成为的人。

sentences.en: Maybe I'm going to tell my kids that I love them and we need to focus on working hard and making friends and those things that are more important in life.
sentences.zh: 也许我要告诉我的孩子们我爱他们，我们需要专注于努力工作、结交朋友以及生活中那些更重要的事情。

sentences.en: Maybe we'll see that cultural shift.
sentences.zh: 也许我们会看到这种文化转变。

sentences.en: After having done all this work looking at the rise of individualism and narcissism, when you go to a party or when you go to a classroom,
sentences.zh: 在做了所有这些关于个人主义和自恋崛起的研讨工作之后，当你去参加派对或走进教室时，

sentences.en: are you actually counting off in your head saying, you know, narcissist, not a narcissist, narcissist, individualist, not an individualist?
sentences.zh: 你会在脑海里数着，你知道的：“自恋狂、不是自恋狂、自恋狂、个人主义者、不是个人主义者”吗？

sentences.en: I mean, are you keeping a running tally as you look at the news about, you know, how these personality traits are manifesting themselves in different people?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当你看着新闻，关注这些个性特征如何在不同的人身上显现时，你是在心里默默记账吗？

sentences.en: Well, sometimes it's glaringly obvious.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有时这是极其显而易见的。

sentences.en: Even people who don't have a background in narcissism, much less psychology, to see displays of narcissism in the current political scene.
sentences.zh: 甚至连没有自恋背景、更不用说心理学背景的人，也能在当前的政治舞台上看到自恋的表现。

sentences.en: But in some cases, yes, there are some – sometimes there are ways that you can spot someone who has these personality traits.
sentences.zh: 但在某些情况下，是的，确实有一些——有时你可以通过某些方法识别出具有这些个性特质的人。

sentences.en: And, you know, some people have said to me, well, you know, is that really useful?
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有些人对我说：“嗯，你知道，这真的有用吗？”

sentences.en: Well, you're just labeling people.
sentences.zh: “嗯，你只是在给别人贴标签。”

sentences.en: But I think the history of psychology suggests that it's not just a label.
sentences.zh: 但我认为心理学的发展史表明，这不仅仅是一个标签。

sentences.en: It's that once you label it, then you can understand it because then you can draw on the huge body of research evidence to know, okay,
sentences.zh: 而是只要你给它贴上标签，你就能理解它，因为这样你就可以利用庞大的研究证据来了解：好吧，

sentences.en: that might help me predict what this person is going to do next.
sentences.zh: 这可能有助于我预测这个人接下来会做什么。

sentences.en: So that, you know, this guy I'm dating, you know, he tends to turn the conversation back around to himself and he likes to brag about his status.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我正在约会的这家伙，你知道的，他总是把话题转回到自己身上，而且他喜欢夸耀自己的地位。

sentences.en: What will happen next?
sentences.zh: 接下来会发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, in three months, he's going to leave you for a younger model.
sentences.zh: 嗯，三个月后，他会为了一个更年轻的款式而甩了你。

sentences.en: That's what's going to happen next.
sentences.zh: 接下来发生的就是这个。

sentences.en: To have an understanding of this trait, among other things.
sentences.zh: 为了理解这一特质，以及其他方面。

sentences.en: Do you apply it in your own life and in your own personal relationships of who you want to have as colleagues or friends?
sentences.zh: 你在自己的生活和个人关系中，是否会用它来挑选你想与之共事的同事或朋友？

sentences.en: I did give my husband the narcissistic personality inventory on our fourth date.
sentences.zh: 我在我们的第四次约会上确实让我丈夫做了自恋人格问卷。

sentences.en: I'm not kidding.
sentences.zh: 我没开玩笑。

sentences.en: I wish I was, but I'm not.
sentences.zh: 我希望我是开玩笑，但我没有。

sentences.en: It was snuck in with a bunch of other personality questionnaires, but I did do that.
sentences.zh: 它是夹在一堆其他性格问卷里偷偷进行的，但我确实这么做了。

sentences.en: And, yeah, he scored low and the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 而且，是的，他得分很低，剩下的就是历史了。

sentences.en: Gene Twenge is a psychologist and the author of the books Generation Me and the Narcissism Epidemic.
sentences.zh: 让·特温格是一位心理学家，也是《我这一代》和《自恋流行病》一书的作者。

sentences.en: This episode of the Hidden Brain podcast was produced by Maggie Penman and edited by Jenny Schmidt.
sentences.zh: 本期《隐藏的大脑》播客由玛吉·彭曼制作，珍妮·施密特剪辑。

sentences.en: Our staff also includes Kara McGurk-Allison, Chris Benderev, and Max Nestrack.
sentences.zh: 我们的团队还包括卡拉·麦格克-艾莉森、克里斯·本德列夫和马克斯·内斯特拉克。

sentences.zh: 你可以在脸书和推特上关注我们的故事。

sentences.zh: 你也可以在当地的公共广播电台收听我的故事。

sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢这一集，考虑在iTunes或你收听播客的任何地方给我们写个评论。

sentences.zh: 这能帮助其他人找到这个节目。

sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆，这里是NPR。
